# Planned Versus Actual

## What this wave planned

The final hardening plan asked for five concrete outcomes: close the half-landed commerce focus lifecycle; strengthen mobile containment and interaction geometry; improve truthful product-specific monetization; extend existing workspace handoff only if real consumer evidence justified it; and finish with release/deployment truth rather than a celebratory guess.

## What was actually completed

### Commerce focus lifecycle

Completed. The original shared commerce surface was fully reread, then rewritten by responsibility rather than partially patched. The first organized rewrite reached 137 lines and was rejected. It was split into `surface.js`, `surfaceShell.js`, `surfaceSections.js`, and `dialogFocus.js`. A dedicated lifecycle test proves native close returns focus, duplicate binding is idempotent, legacy focus APIs fall back, and missing launchers fail safely.

### Mobile commerce geometry

Completed. The old sheet had a 40px close control and a non-wrapping footer that could collide with the full-width mobile Favorite control. The first full rewrite reached 140 lines and was rejected. It was split into `sheet.css`, `sheetLayout.css`, and `sheetContent.css`, with a dedicated CSS contract test. The current layout enforces a 44px close target, 44px Wallet/account links, safe-area left/right/bottom treatment, horizontal containment, wrapping footer behavior, and narrow-screen link layout.

### Product-aware Radiance positioning

Completed without changing fulfillment. All 80 live Radiance actions remain 25 credits, permanent durable entitlements, handler-backed, and server-owned. Offer descriptions now name the actual product. Games explicitly state cosmetic-only and no gameplay advantage. Apps explicitly state purely decorative and core functionality unchanged.

### Wallet settlement health

Completed earlier in this hardening sequence and preserved through every subsequent regression. The authenticated current-account health route is GET-only, text/plain, no-store, read-only under the Wallet lock, identity-free, and detects stale holds / contradictory execution topology while recognizing legitimate `already_owned` deduplication.

### Retention and catalog continuity

Completed earlier in this hardening sequence and preserved. Product-route-only Recent/Favorite memory remains bounded, local, non-content-bearing, and browser-proven. Apps/Games catalog ordering/decorations remain green.

### Startup performance

Measured, not cosmetically hidden. The isolated server reached HTTP readiness in roughly eight seconds while explicit lifecycle awaits consumed only milliseconds. Module loading—not DB/auth awaits—is the dominant cost. Request-time families were identified, but the remaining safe optimization boundary crosses legacy config/Auth/DosDB infrastructure. No fake post-bind readiness trick was introduced.

### Workspace/embed handoff

Architecture confirmed, exhaustive consumer audit incomplete. Existing workspace launch descriptors and versioned embed protocol already provide path confinement, origin/direction checks, and typed launch destinations. A duplicate weaker handoff protocol was deliberately not added. Recursive consumer searches repeatedly stalled and remain an audit item.

### Deployment

The public Awtsmoos.com deployment is live and independently verified. The local hardened checkout is not blindly pushed because the working tree contains 1,510 dirty paths and local committed HEAD is 3 commits ahead / 26 behind `origin/main`. Production is SHA-locked through GitHub Actions and a Hetzner hard-reset deployment, so promoting this tree wholesale would risk unrelated concurrent work.

## What remains honestly incomplete

- Prove a coherent clean release candidate from current `origin/main` that includes all tracked and untracked dependencies used by the hardened local graph.
- Run the production quality workflow against that isolated candidate before any main push.
- Finish exhaustive workspace-launch consumer mapping.
- Design a coherent non-JSON legacy config/Auth/DosDB migration before aggressive startup-lazy-load work.

The current green local product is materially stronger; the remaining work is release isolation and legacy migration, not a broken commerce or catalog core.
